scope: Proposition A.2 (Finite ordering transfer) of the manuscript “The Unique Games Theorem” (preprints/The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 04d0290a9cb7ee81), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 46. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix k ≥ 2 and ∅ ̸= Π ⊊ Sk, put ρΠ = |Π|/k!, and fix 0 < δ < (1 − ρΠ)/2. There are integers q, H ≥ 1 and positive rationals ζ, ν < 1, depending only on k, Π, δ, with the following property for every fixed integer R ≥ 1. Let Φ = (A, B, E) be a nonempty explicit unweighted simple bipartite Unique Games instance over [R], oriented from A to B, whose common left degree h satisfies h ≥ H and q | h. There is a deterministic transformation, polynomial in the explicit size of Φ for fixed R, producing an explicit list of Π-ordering constraints on distinct variables within each constraint, with nonnegative rational weights, each encoded by a binary numerator and a positive binary denominator, summing to one. If some labeling strongly satisfies at least (1 − ζ)|A| left vertices, then OPTΠ(I) ≥ 1 − δ. If val(Φ) ≤ ν, then OPTΠ(I) ≤ ρΠ + δ. The constants q, H, ζ, ν are independent of both R and h.
